fields.statement: QA built 3bcbde2fe to $TMPDIR/rhiza-x and main 5180b25eb to $TMPDIR/rhiza-main. On a scratch repo with a landed base, in-flight A (forged verifies link, forged dangling @{01ZZ...} text ref, ref to a since-retired node), B depends-on A and edits A's node, and C whose set on store is stale after a record retire, rhiza check reported the bad in-flight link, the broken text ref, the retired-ref warning and C's what-if conflict once each, exit 1; human and --json output were byte-identical to main, also under GOMAXPROCS=1. rhiza check --json on ~/code/rhiza (5180b25eb), on this worktree and on a fresh init repo (unrendered and rendered) were byte-identical to main.

QA exercised AsIsSeed, ToBeFrom and WhatIfFrom through the built rhiza check (3bcbde2fe): on the scratch repo with dependent, stale and bad-link in-flight change sets and on ~/code/rhiza, every in-flight and to-be finding and the whole --json report matched main 5180b25eb (which uses ToBe and WhatIf) byte for byte, so the seed views gave the same models and problems.

QA ran the built rhiza check (3bcbde2fe) on a scratch log with an unreadable entry (chmod 000), an entry that does not decode and an entry copied under a non-matching file name: each was one fail log finding in path order, with the fold findings after, and human and --json output under default GOMAXPROCS and GOMAXPROCS=1 were byte-identical to main 5180b25eb. On ~/code/rhiza, check --json matched main byte for byte; main took 14.14 s, the branch 7.46 s (6.80 s human, 11.09 s at GOMAXPROCS=1); the 5 s miss is ruled (check-time-gap-carried).
